## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Tikapuggalapaññatti* is the third chapter of the *Puggalapaññatti* within the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Following the mātika of the treatise, it defines and classifies various personality types and human dispositions into groups of three [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records two modern translations of the text in two languages [SuttaCentral].
The text draws extensively upon material found across the Sutta Piṭaka. SuttaCentral identifies passage-level parallels with the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 1.1, *Puggalakathā*) and the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (Ps 1.5, *Vimokkhakathā*) [SuttaCentral]. It also shares content or is referenced in numerous suttas, prominent among them discourses from the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* Tikanipāta—including the *Gilānasutta* (AN 3.22), *Vajirūpamasutta* (AN 3.25), *Sevitabbasutta* (AN 3.26), *Gūthabhāṇīsutta* (AN 3.28), *Avakujjasutta* (AN 3.30), *Potthakasutta* (AN 3.99), and *Lekhasutta* (AN 3.132)—as well as the *Majjhima Nikāya* (MN 41 and MN 114) and the *Niddesa* (Mnd 7, Mnd 14, and Cnd 22) [SuttaCentral].
This close relationship with the Sutta literature is reflected in DharmaNexus's text-reuse analysis, which detects 4,642 matching segments across 158 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. By far its largest text-reuse partner is the *Tikanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (498 matches totaling over 104,000 characters), along with significant internal formulaic reuse across other sections of the *Puggalapaññatti* (such as Pp 2.4, Pp 2.1, and Pp 2.2) and commentary in the *Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns passages of the text with Sanskrit works (including the *Udānavarga*, *Yogācārabhūmi*'s *Śrāvakabhūmi*, and fragments of an *Ekottarāgama*), Tibetan translations (such as the *Udānavargavivaraṇa*, *Mahāparinirvāṇasūtra*, and *Pradīpadānīyasūtra*), and Chinese Āgamas (*Saṃyuktāgama*, T 99, and *Madhyamāgama*, T 26) [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
